advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In _warn_if_verify_cannot_resolve, distinguish 'checked and resolvable' from 'guard failed to run' (e.g. log the exception at WARNING or record that the check could not execute) instead of a silent DEBUG skip.
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:322-325: `        logger.debug("op-cert public-counterpart guard skipped (best-effort; key_path=%s)", ...)`

ABSENCE: no WARNING/liveness signal distinguishes 'guard ran and key is resolvable' from 'guard threw before it could compare', so the guard's silence fails open — the same silent-deferred-failure class the guard exists to surface.
advisory.finding: The mint-time guard _warn_if_verify_cannot_resolve swallows any internal failure (from _read_opcert_pub or _opcert_own_public_keys) into a DEBUG-level log and returns silently, so a crashed guard is indistinguishable from a 'checked and clean' healthy path. The WARNING that surfaces the 879b divergence is only emitted when the resolver comparison completes successfully; if resolving the signer's own pub or the own-key set raises, no WARNING is produced and the divergence goes unsurfaced.
scenarios: A transient filesystem/permission error reading the signer's .pub or the own-key set during minting: the divergence goes unwarned and the operator sees nothing.

evidence: diff adds `"opcert": getattr(mcp, _OPCERT_STATUS_ATTR, {"bound": False, "expected": False}),` to the /health response
search of tests for `_rebar_opcert_status` / `_OPCERT_STATUS_ATTR` returns (no matches)
tests/unit/test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose.py:400 run_mcp test asserts only seen['transport'/'binding'/'push_mode'], never the stashed opcert status

Named violating input: run_mcp(server, SimpleNamespace(transport='stdio'), opcert_binding=_Signer(unpinned_key, ENV_ID)) with pinning configured should leave getattr(server, _OPCERT_STATUS_ATTR) reporting matched=False, but no test asserts the attribute is set at all.
advisory.finding: The run_mcp wiring that stashes opcert_signing_status onto the server for the /health 'opcert' field is untested: no test asserts setattr(server, _OPCERT_STATUS_ATTR, ...) actually records the probe result, so a regression dropping or mis-naming the stash (leaving /health reporting the default {bound:False,expected:False}) would go undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm surfacing `env_id` and raw resolution-error text in the unauthenticated /health `opcert` field is intended, matching the accepted store_status precedent (or redact error text).
evidence: register_health_route docstring: 'the route lives on the Starlette app OUTSIDE the auth and transport-security middleware — an unauthenticated probe gets 200.'

opcert_signing_status records `status["error"] = str(exc)` (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py) and load_trusted_environments raises TrustedEnvError(f"cannot read trusted-environments config {path}: {exc}") (src/rebar/attest/trusted_env.py:79) — so filesystem paths can reach the error string.

PRECEDENT/GUARD: the SAME endpoint already exposes `store_status()` which returns `path` (a filesystem path) and error text unauthenticated (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:299-300), an established accepted pattern — so this new field follows existing precedent rather than introducing a new exposure class.
advisory.finding: The unauthenticated /health endpoint's new `opcert` field surfaces the signer principal (`env_id`) and, on a resolution fault, an `error` string derived from `str(exc)` which can include trusted-environment config filesystem paths (TrustedEnvError messages embed the config path) to an unauthenticated probe.

evidence: Test: `caplog.clear()` then `_write_trusted_env(store, ENV_ID, _pub_of(key))  # now the signer IS pinned` then `assert [r for r in caplog.records if r.levelno == logging.WARNING] == []`

Production swallow path: `except Exception:  # a health check must never abort boot` / `logging.getLogger("rebar").debug("startup op-cert check skipped", exc_info=True)` (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:385-386) — a crash produces zero WARNING records, indistinguishable from the intended silent-pinned pass.

ABSENCE rationale: the second half lacks a liveness anchor (e.g. asserting opcert_signing_status(...)['matched'] is True on the re-pinned signer) that would prove the silent result came from the healthy matched path rather than a swallowed exception.
advisory.finding: The 'silent when pinned' half of test_startup_opcert_check_warns_only_when_degraded asserts an ABSENCE (zero WARNING records) from run_startup_opcert_check, which swallows any non-RemovedInputError into a DEBUG log; the same zero-warning result is produced whether the check ran cleanly-silent (matched, healthy) or crashed and was swallowed. The half has no producer-liveness anchor (no assertion that the pinned-path status was actually computed with matched=True / no error) so it cannot distinguish a genuine silent-pinned pass from a swallowed-fault pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: Before the final `assert [...] == []`, add `assert _mcp_health.opcert_signing_status(_Signer(key, ENV_ID), repo_root=str(store))['matched'] is True` to establish that the pinned path resolves cleanly (no swallowed error) rather than trusting the absence of a warning alone.
